subsystems.name: Reaction vessel
subsystems.role: holds the starting mixture under controlled conditions, often as a continuous flow rather than a sealed flask.
parts: heated or cooled channels (from below 0 °C up to ~100 °C)

subsystems.name: Starting mixture and medium
subsystems.role: the plausible feedstock — simple molecules rather than biological ones.
parts: water, hydrogen cyanide, formaldehyde, ammonia, hydrogen sulfide
dissolved phosphate, borate and metal salts
acid or alkaline buffers setting pH

subsystems.name: Mineral surfaces and catalysts
subsystems.role: concentrate dilute products and steer reactions toward the useful ones.

subsystems.name: Sample handling and separation
subsystems.role: pull small samples out of the mixture without disturbing it.

subsystems.name: Analytical detection
subsystems.role: identify what formed, at micromolar to millimolar concentrations, among hundreds of side products.

subsystems.name: Network modelling
subsystems.role: turns lists of detected molecules into a map of which reactions feed which.

buildSteps.title: Pick a plausible world
buildSteps.detail: Decide which environment is being imitated — a warm pond with wetting and drying cycles, an alkaline hydrothermal vent, or an icy moon's ocean — because that fixes the temperature, pH and minerals.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the feedstock
buildSteps.detail: Prepare a simple mixture of gases and salts that could have arisen from atmospheric chemistry, impacts or mineral reactions, and confirm its composition by analysis.

buildSteps.title: Set up a closed reactor
buildSteps.detail: Build an oxygen-free flow system with pumps, heated zones and a UV window, so the mixture can be held far from equilibrium for days or weeks.

buildSteps.title: Introduce minerals and catalysts
buildSteps.detail: Add suspended mineral grains or packed mineral beds so surfaces can concentrate and orient molecules.

buildSteps.title: Run and sample over time
buildSteps.detail: Continuously flow the mixture and withdraw small samples at intervals, tracking how the population of molecules changes rather than only its final state.

buildSteps.title: Identify and quantify products
buildSteps.detail: Separate the mixture by chromatography and identify each compound by mass spectrometry and NMR, measuring yield against a known standard.

buildSteps.title: Map the reaction network
buildSteps.detail: Feed the results into network models to see which pathways dominate, which intermediates are dead ends, and where the system remains 'dirty'.

buildSteps.title: Test for selection
buildSteps.detail: Ask whether any products accumulate, self-assemble into vesicles, or template their own formation — the step from chemistry toward biology.

buildSteps.title: Repeat under other conditions
buildSteps.detail: Rerun the same network with different minerals, pH or energy sources to see which starting points converge on the same molecules.

prerequisites.why: prebiotic mixtures are complex and dilute; without precise identification no network can be mapped.
credible routes to nucleotides, amino acids and lipids exist separately, but rarely share one set of conditions.
holding mixtures far from equilibrium for long periods, while sampling them, is still a young technique.
real surfaces are messy and hard to characterise, so their role is understood only roughly.
getting molecules to assemble into growing, dividing compartments is demonstrated in simplified systems only.

pathway.milestone: separate reaction networks for nucleotides, amino acids and lipids, mapped with modern analytics
pathway.unlocks: a shared language for comparing competing origin-of-life scenarios.

pathway.milestone: networks that overlap — one plausible environment producing precursors of all three molecule classes together
pathway.unlocks: a coherent chemical story for early Earth rather than a patchwork.

pathway.milestone: demonstrated selection and self-replication, such as an RNA-like polymer that copies itself inside a simple compartment
pathway.unlocks: a laboratory model of the transition from chemistry to biology.

pathway.milestone: a general account of which environments and minerals drive the emergence of heredity
pathway.unlocks: targeted biosignature searches on Mars, Europa and Enceladus, and better rules for synthetic biology.
